prompt:
Photorealistic rear-view portrait of one adult person.

Head, neck, upper torso, shoulders, upper back, and enough torso
landmarks must be visible to judge the endpoint of the hair.

Both shoulders must be clearly visible.

Neutral natural posture.

Simple uncluttered indoor background.

Natural photographic lighting.

Realistic individual hair strands.

Realistic hair volume.

Realistic hair silhouette.

Natural-looking hair texture.

High-detail natural photography.

The image is intended for visual taxonomy calibration.

The hair endpoint must be clearly visible.

The relationship between the hair endpoint and the anatomical
landmarks of the body must be visually judgeable.

The camera framing must preserve enough of the upper torso and
back to determine whether the hair ends above, at, or below
important body landmarks.

Medium-brown wavy hair with natural subtle variation.

Do not crop the shoulders.

Do not crop the hair ends.

Do not hide the hair behind clothing.

Do not use an extreme camera angle.

Do not use an extreme close-up.

Do not create an illustration or painting.

Do not add accessories that obscure the hair.

Do not add text or annotations.


IMPORTANT HAIR-LENGTH REQUIREMENT:

Target length taxonomy category: VERY_SHORT

Operational landmark:
ABOVE_EAR


Required visual relationship:
hair ends clearly above the ears or around the upper-ear region; no substantial hair reaches the jawline; the full hair endpoint should be clearly visible


Taxonomy definition:
Hair remains very close to the head, with the visible hair ending clearly above the ears or around the upper-ear region.


The hair endpoint and its relationship to the visible anatomical
landmarks must be visually obvious enough for an independent
human evaluator to determine the intended category from the
image alone.

Do not exaggerate the hair length beyond the specified category.

Do not allow the hair to cross into another length category.

The image must contain sufficient visible body landmarks for
independent human verification.
